tools.name: mcp_liveness_check
tools.description:
Makes one handshake with an MCP server's endpoint — `server/discover` at protocol revision
2026-07-28, then `initialize` for a server on the older revision — with no credential, and
reports what a stock client gets. The server is named either by its exact official-registry
`name`, or by its endpoint

tools.name: mcp_liveness_explain_outcomes
tools.description: Returns the six outcomes this server can report — usable, needs_credential, charged, unreachable, local_only and not_listed — what each means for an agent choosing a server from the registry, and the usual next move for each. A static reference: it makes no network request and its answer never chang

findings.detail: Description of "mcp_liveness_check_auth" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "mcp_liveness_check" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet:
before: "Given a server's exact name in the official MCP registry, make one `initialize` call to
the endpoint its listing names and report what a client with no credential gets.

Outcomes: `usable` (it connected and negotiated a protocol version), `needs_credential`
(401 or 403 — the answer then says whether" → after: "Makes one handshake with an MCP server's endpoint — `server/discover` at protocol revision
2026-07-28, then `initialize` for a server on the older revision — with no credential, and
reports what a stock client gets. The server is named either by its exact official-registry
`name`, or by its endpoint"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
